episodes.161025: Isolated thunderstorms developed on the afternoon of the second under a very hot low level atmosphere. One of these storms produced a microburst near Brownfield (Terry County) as it moved over a Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet. A peak wind gust of 76 mph was measured by this mesonet near Brownfield.
episodes.161030: A thunderstorm strengthened as it moved to the east-southeast across southern St. Lucie and northeastern Martin counties, eventually producing a waterspout just after it moved offshore of northeastern Martin county during the late afternoon hours.
episodes.161656: A tropical wave moved across the area. The associated moisture along with strong daytime heating and local effects generated enhanced shower and thunderstorm activity, mainly across the north-central municipalities of Puerto Rico.
episodes.161693: Afternoon and evening showers over leeward parts of the Big Island of Hawaii became heavy after daytime heating and enhancement provided by a nearby upper level disturbance.  The rain caused small stream and drainage ditch flooding, and ponding on roadways.  No serious injuries or property damage were reported.
episodes.162107: A front settled across southeast Georgia and lingered across northeast Florida. Diurnal instability combined with a moist airmass triggered scattered showers and isolated storms along the meandering front, some of which produced heavy rainfall.
episodes.162578: Residual monsoon moisture paired with moderate instability led to afternoon thunderstorms across the higher terrain of southeast Utah. One storm in San Juan County produced a funnel cloud.
episodes.163018: A long tracking supercell produced severe weather in southeast Idaho.
episodes.163107: Unorganized thunderstorms developed in an environment favorable for downbursts, with one report of severe winds received with a storm in northwest OK on the 3rd.
episodes.163185: Isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms occurred across the central mountains and into the Pikes Peak region during this period, with rainfall amounts generally staying on the lighter side. A few higher amounts above one inch were observed across the Pikes Peak region though.
episodes.163192: Heavy rain led to a localized flood.
episodes.163204: The remnants of Ida produced widespread flooding along with instances of flash flooding across the area. Tropical moisture infiltrated the area and there were moderate amounts of instability as well. This combined with the lift provided from the remnants of Ida led to heavy rainfall during this time. Rainfall amounts averaged around 1-3 near and east of Interstate 95, with amounts around 4 to 8 inches across portions of northern and central Maryland. Excess runoff from the heavy rainfall led to river flooding as well.
episodes.163255: Severe thunderstorms produced hail up to quarter size and wind gusts to 65 mph over portions of Arapahoe, Jefferson and Douglas counties.
episodes.163286: Two rounds of storms occurred late on 9/2 and early on 9/3, producing isolated wind damage and flash flooding.
episodes.163391: Heavy rainfall moved across portions of central and south central Kansas during the early morning hours of September 3rd.  Rainfall amounts of 2 to 4 inches occurred.
episodes.163420: Several rounds of thunderstorms brought severe weather hazards to the state of Utah, including flash flooding in southern and eastern Utah, and damaging winds, hail, and a tornado in Northern Utah.
episodes.163421: Thunderstorms brought severe wind gusts to portions of southwestern Wyoming near Evanston.
episodes.163595: Isolated severe storms moved out of the Oklahoma Panhandle with a few hail reports over an inch in diameter. There was enough differential heating across southwestern counties allowing for CAPE values over 1500 J/kg. Mid-level lapse rates were relatively low with warm upper level temperatures in this area. This prevented more widespread convection becoming organized as the afternoon progressed. These storms diminished quickly becoming more of a widespread rain event leading to heavier downpours with relatively slow movement. Precipitation amounts of 2-3 inches overnight for northern counties along the single band of heavy precipitation that lead to a flash flood warning as well.
episodes.163763: An upper level shortwave trough and an attendant cold front combined to produce widespread thunderstorms that moved relatively slowly.  PW values of nearly 2 inches contributed to heavy rainfall amounts.

events.narrative: Hail up to 1 inch in diameter fell in Salt Lake City.
Hail up to 3/4 of an inch in diameter fell in East Mill Creek.

A tornado first touched down in North Salt Lake at Redwood Road and 900 W around 628 PM MDT. The tornado moved to the northeast through a mix of industrial and residential areas. The tornado produced EF0 damage (winds 65 to 85 MPH) to numerous trees and several homes in the Cloverdale neighborhood. The tornado continued to move off to the northeast, producing more EF0 damage to the Woods Cross Public Works building and a nearby construction site. The tornado reached peak intensity along 1100 W, producing EF1 damage (winds 86 to 110 MPH) where it uprooted a healthy mature tree and leaned a wooden power pole. The tornado continued to the north, weakening, but still producing EF0 damage before lifting off the ground.||The tornado then made a second touchdown in a field near 800 W where it produced EF0 damage to a business in the area and began moving northward along 800 W. Tree damage and minor property damage indicative of an EF0 tornado was widespread along this swath. Large diameter tree limbs (in excess of 12 inches) were broken off and deposited throughout the area. The tornado then dissipated in the area of 1500 S and Interstate 15 around 634 PM MDT.||The rating for this tornado is EF1 with winds as high as 110 MPH. The tornado had an intermittent track length of about 2 miles over 7 minutes and a max-width of approximately 350 yards with an average width of approximately 150 yards.
